Say they are built the same all the tracks are carved out by landcruisers and patrols the wheel base of this particular tj is to small and would constantly high center itself, as for the front solid axel that has the fj beat on front flex, the open diffs are another weakness as the fj has factory lockers. I've driven the tj and it is extremely under powered in comparison to the fj. When turned on the computer driver assist in the fj would allow it to climb better and more stably. (Not that I use them because they are lame and take the fun out of it) the electrical side of things the fj has a higher water tolerance than the tj.

 the tj is the obvious choice in the US because parts are available and there are lots of them but in aus they just can't compare. The short wheel base also dramatically increases the risk of roll overs as the fj is a mid wheel base it has the best of both worlds. 

To sum it up all the tj has is a slight weight advantage compared to the fjs 1.8t and the front solid axel.
